novelty_gate.candidate_contribution: A leakage-safe, subject- and trial-exclusive, one-way ability-associated population-shift benchmark on InclusiveHAR v4, with source-only model selection, explicit activity-realization ontology, matched strong baselines, participant-level lower-tail and calibration evidence, and an auditable one-time target evaluation.
novelty_gate.caveat: This is a scoped search result and candidate distinction, not proof of novelty and not authorization to claim first, fairness, clinical validity, or publishability.

works.title: InclusiveHAR: A smartphone-based dataset for human activity recognition across diverse physical abilities
works.key_boundary: The paper already reports an author-described non-disabled-only training scenario, but split and target provenance are insufficient to verify a participant/trial-exclusive locked zero-shot protocol.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones
works.key_boundary: Conventional 30-participant population and subject-separated official split; no disability metadata, and stairs/body-acceleration semantics are not automatically compatible with InclusiveHAR. The current catalog's CC BY 4.0 label conflicts with the embedded Version 1.0 non-commercial notice; both must be preserved as unresolved and the data must not be redistributed or relicensed.

works.title: Promoting fairness in activity recognition algorithms for patient's monitoring and evaluation systems in healthcare
works.key_boundary: Direct disability/fairness prior using Kinect skeleton shoulder exercises; not smartphone inertial or a locked source-only population-shift benchmark.

works.title: HAROOD: A Benchmark for Out-of-distribution Generalization in Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic HAR OOD benchmark claim; it has no ability-defined target, and oracle model selection is diagnostic.

works.title: BenchHAR: Benchmarking Self-Supervised Learning for Generalizable Sensor-based Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic SSL-generalization benchmark; no ability-defined cohort or participant lower-tail/calibration endpoint.

works.title: WHAR Arena: Benchmarking the State of the Art in Efficient Wearable Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts generic standardized accuracy-efficiency comparison; no ability-defined one-way target.

works.title: Generalizable Sensor-Based Activity Recognition via Categorical Concept Invariant Learning
works.key_boundary: Direct predecessor for category-conditioned invariant feature/logit learning; must be compared with MoRe-HAR.

works.title: In Shift and In Variance: Assessing the Robustness of HAR Deep Learning Models Against Variability
works.key_boundary: Direct prior for person/device/position/orientation shift, but not ability-associated source-to-target generalization.

works.title: STORM: Hardware-Aware Tiny Transformer Co-Design for Low-Power Inertial Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts generic tiny-Transformer, sensor-fault, and edge-co-design claims; ability by reliability remains secondary.

works.title: Rotation-Invariant Multi-IMU Activity Recognition under Independent Per-Location Orientation Shifts
works.key_boundary: Preempts exact rotation-invariant multi-IMU novelty; not an ability-defined shift study.

works.title: Inertia-1: An Open Exploration of Wearable Motion Foundation Models
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic wearable foundation-model-scale study; its pretraining scale is out of scope and it has no ability-defined target.

works.title: Learning Disentangled Behaviour Patterns for Wearable-based Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: High conceptual collision: BPD already separates activity behaviour from personal style/environmental nuisance and reports participant-level F1.

works.title: CMD-HAR: Cross-Modal Disentanglement for Wearable Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Further invalidates generic disentanglement novelty; ratio-only split documentation does not establish subject exclusivity for all datasets.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition Dataset for Pedestrians with Mobility Disabilities
works.key_boundary: Strong mobility-aid HAR benchmark with 120 participants and user-independent evaluation, but activities are simulated modes/aids rather than same-activity generalization to an independently recruited disabled cohort.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition from Smartphone Sensor Data for Clinical Trials
works.key_boundary: Includes healthy controls and people with MS, but GaitLab development mixes both cohorts and the full everyday-activity endpoint is evaluated only on healthy Roche participants.

works.title: Activity Recognition for Persons With Stroke Using Mobile Phone Technology
works.key_boundary: Direct smartphone healthy-to-stroke transfer precedent; rules out first healthy-to-disabled smartphone evaluation.

works.title: Activity Recognition in Individuals Walking With Assistive Devices: Benefits of Device-Specific Models
works.key_boundary: Direct healthy-global-to-assistive-device-user evaluation; rules out first assistive-device or healthy-to-disabled transfer claim.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition of Individuals with Lower Limb Amputation in Free-Living Conditions: A Pilot Study
works.key_boundary: Direct non-impaired-to-lower-limb-amputee transfer failure; strongly narrows cross-ability novelty language.
